adaptations.rationale: Preserves the frozen Grok 0.18 React renderer structure while adapting shipping Fabushi contracts only: browser-login status application is monotonic so a late logging-in acknowledgement cannot overwrite a newer logged-in observation; the root exposes stable Agent-shell markers used by product parity acceptance; empty sidebar-section records fall back to Grok visible-Agent ordering; and complete-roster reconciliation settles an unselected account on the first visible Agent. These adaptations also publish the live sidebar width to the shell so the recovered WindowChrome drag carrier does not overlap Fabushi Agent header controls; the sidebar header remains the local drag surface and its controls are explicit no-drag regions. They keep authentication real through cursorAccount.login/getStatus and keep roster/selection state on the production Coordinator path rather than introducing a parallel renderer. It also preserves optimistic user-message text and committed attachment metadata while correlated authoritative message/attachment echoes settle, so the live transcript does not drop attachment chips between send acceptance and durable echo. Authoritative transcript baselines, updates, and appends are reconciled by message id and client nonce while unioning committed attachment metadata, so transport ordering or a late durable snapshot cannot erase a user's attachment chip after send acceptance. Initial openAgentTail completion is also reconciled with entries that arrived while the initial page request was in flight, preventing a stale first-page response from erasing an optimistic or newly echoed attachment-bearing turn. Transcript feed snapshots also retain only unresolved pending-* user turns that have not yet been correlated by id/clientNonce, so a late empty or stale authoritative baseline cannot erase the optimistic turn between submit acceptance and its durable echo; ordinary non-pending rows remain fully baseline-authoritative. The shipping renderer now also owns the recovered Grok sidebar multi-selection composition: modifier/range selection, clear, and bulk move-to-existing/new-section callbacks are wired to renderer state and the account-scoped sidebarSectionsStore, so the byte-identical sidebar selection UI is reachable without a legacy shell.

Keeps Grok 0.18 Agent projection/filter/sort semantics while accepting the shipping Mahayana Coordinator agents event envelope { agents: [...] } in addition to the frozen direct array form. The adaptation is limited to transport normalization at the renderer projection boundary; Agent identity, hidden state, activity and ordering continue through the frozen Grok projection logic. It also normalizes authoritative Mahayana transcript echoes that carry Grok attachment contexts on user messages, preserving committed path/name/MIME/size metadata for mixed and attachment-only sends without relying on optimistic renderer state.

Preserves the frozen Grok 0.18 account-scoped composer draft store while adapting a shipping race exposed by real desktop attachment staging: a late persistence restore must not overwrite a draft mutation that occurred while the read was in flight. A monotonic mutation revision fences both pre-read and post-read restore settlement without changing account generation semantics, persistence format, or normal draft equality rules. The explicit .ts model import makes this recovered module executable under the Node 24 strip-types contract-test runner while remaining valid under the desktop Bundler TypeScript configuration.

Preserves the frozen Grok 0.18 thin preload boundary while adapting Fabushi's native attachment IPC contract: renderer Uint8Array payloads are encoded to the native bytesBase64 field, rich native staging results are normalized to the recovered {ok,path} contract, and rich committed attachment records are normalized to string paths. Commit requests carry path/name pairs as native items so file names survive the staging-to-committed transition. This keeps binary conversion and native response-shape adaptation in the preload bridge instead of leaking native IPC details into the React renderer.

Preserves the frozen Grok 0.18 TipTap composer structure while adapting the shipping scope-switch transaction fence to the real ProseMirror browser-input contract. In the shipping Electron renderer, ordinary contenteditable typing is not guaranteed to carry transaction.getMeta("uiEvent"), so the frozen fence could keep accepting DOM edits while suppressing every onChange after opening a newly materialized Agent: the prompt appeared on screen but the React draft remained empty and the Send message action never rendered. The adaptation keeps stale pre-scope transactions fenced, releases ownership on the browser beforeinput event before TipTap creates the real user-edit transaction, and explicitly releases the same fence for voice/dictation insertText commands. It does not alter Agent identity, draft persistence, submission, or Coordinator/Host ownership; focused Electron acceptance proves a pure-text turn reaches the canonical recovered composer and shipping Mahayana path.

Preserves Grok attachment-gateway behavior while removing a forbidden Electron-main dependency on the legacy TypeScript Host attachment service. Link metadata now crosses the existing Coordinator main leg, and bounded preview-image handling lives in shared media code. This keeps Electron Main, Coordinator and Host as independent Grok-shaped processes while retaining the same attachment/link-preview contract.

Preserves Grok MCP/OAuth composition while moving the shared Fabushi data-root resolver out of the legacy Host TypeScript tree. Electron Main no longer imports Host implementation code merely to locate persistent data, preserving the Host process boundary without changing MCP OAuth behavior.

Keeps the frozen Grok attachment manager semantics while sourcing data-root and path reanchoring from the shared Node boundary rather than legacy Host TypeScript. This is a dependency-direction adaptation only; attachment lifecycle and path semantics remain owned by Electron Main.

Preserves Grok Electron-main Coordinator auxiliary wiring while resolving the Fabushi data directory through shared Node infrastructure instead of importing legacy Host TypeScript. The Coordinator itself remains the independent Rust Mahayana process; this adaptation only cleans the Electron-side dependency edge.

Preserves Grok development box-recreate behavior while moving the data-root dependency to the shared Node layer. This prevents the development control plane from retaining a second legacy Host runtime dependency.

Keeps Grok media-protocol behavior and changes only the path-reanchoring dependency from legacy Host TypeScript to the shared data-root utility, preserving Electron Main ownership of privileged media protocol handling.

Preserves the frozen Grok production binding graph while cutting two legacy Host-TypeScript imports: local-exec daemon protocol ownership is now in Electron Main and the data-root resolver is shared. The actual local-exec supervision still belongs to Mahayana Coordinator, so this adaptation strengthens rather than collapses the Grok process boundary.

Preserves Grok desktop user-data bootstrap semantics while moving Fabushi data-root helpers from legacy Host TypeScript into the shared Node layer, so Electron startup no longer depends on a parallel Host implementation.

Preserves Grok startup data-root migration behavior while replacing legacy Host path/lock imports with shared data-root utilities and an Electron-main host-process identity seam. This lets migration safely recognize the shipping Mahayana Host without retaining the old Host runtime implementation.

Keeps Grok local-tool approval persistence semantics while moving the common data-root lookup to shared Node infrastructure. The shipping local-exec lifecycle is supervised by the independent Rust Coordinator; this TypeScript compatibility module no longer owns or imports a Host runtime path.

Preserves the Cursor backend path but deliberately removes the legacy in-process TypeScript provider-session fallback. Any non-Cursor provider must route through Mahayana Coordinator and the independent Host/Runner pipeline, enforcing the required Grok Coordinator/Host/Runner fault and responsibility boundaries rather than keeping a second inference runtime.

Extends the frozen Coordinator-main RPC contract with fetchLinkMetadata so Electron attachment previews cross the Coordinator boundary instead of calling legacy Host TypeScript directly. Request/reply ownership and transport remain on the existing Coordinator protocol; no parallel channel is introduced.
